'''Nathalie Michelle Sinclair''' (born 1970)<ref>Birth year from [http://www.isni.org/isni/0000000109617566 ISNI authority control file], retrieved 2018-12-02.</ref> is a Canadian researcher in [[mathematics education]] who holds the [[Canada Research Chair]] in Tangible Mathematics Learning at [[Simon Fraser University]] in [[Vancouver]].<ref>[http://www.chairs-chaires.gc.ca/chairholders-titulaires/profile-eng.aspx?profileId=2823 Nathalie Sinclair], Canada Research Chairs, retrieved 2016-07-08.</ref>

==Early life and education==
Sinclair was born in [[Grenoble]], the daughter of Canadian academics who were on sabbatical there; she grew up in [[Calgary]]. She began her undergraduate studies at [[McGill University]] in business, but quickly switched to mathematics, and then earned a master's degree with Len Berggren at Simon Fraser on the [[history of mathematics]] and [[mathematics in medieval Islam]].<ref name="face"/>

She became a middle school teacher of mathematics and French on [[Bowen Island]].<ref name="face">{{citation|url=http://mathcentral.uregina.ca/humanface/careers/profiles/nathaliesinclair.pdf|title=Nathalie Sinclair|work=Mathematics with a Human Face|publisher=Math Central, Mathematics and Statistics and Mathematics Education, [[University of Regina]]|accessdate=2016-07-08}}.</ref> Sinclair then earned her Ph.D. in 2002 from [[Queen's University at Kingston]], under the joint supervision of Peter Taylor of the Department of Mathematics and Statistics and William Higginson of the Faculty of Education.<ref>{{mathgenealogy|id=67817}}</ref>

==Career==
[[File:Nathalie.sinclairRSC.SFU.jpg|thumb|left|Sinclair in 2017]]

In 2003, Sinclair accepted a joint appointment in the College of Natural Sciences and the College of Education at [[Michigan State University]].<ref>{{cite web |title=College Welcomes New faculty |url=http://www.educ.msu.edu/neweducator/fall03/newfaculty.htm |website=educ.msu.edu |accessdate=November 12, 2019 |date=Fall 2003}}</ref>

In 2014, Sinclair and [[Nicholas Jackiw]] developed a mathematical app targeted at children ages three to eight. The purpose of the app is to teach children math through "hands-on" learning.<ref>{{cite web |author1=Allen M. Quinn |title=New approach to math gives kids 'hands-on' experience with numbers |url=https://www.sfu.ca/sfunews/stories/2019/08/new-approach-to-math-gives-kids--hands-on--experience-with-numbe.html |website=sfu.ca |accessdate=November 12, 2019 |date=August 8, 2019}}</ref> Two years later, she was named a Tier 2 [[Canada Research Chair]] in Tangible Mathematics Learning.<ref>{{cite web |title=Nathalie Sinclair |url=https://www.chairs-chaires.gc.ca/chairholders-titulaires/profile-eng.aspx?profileId=2823&pedisable=true |website=chairs-chaires.gc.ca |accessdate=November 12, 2019}}</ref>

In March 2017, Sinclair was named Canada's Mathematics Ambassador by Partners in Research for her contributions to the field of mathematics.<ref>{{cite web |title=SFU education professor Nathalie Sinclair named 2017 Mathematics Ambassador by Partners in Research |url=https://www.sfu.ca/sfunews/stories/2017/03/sfu-education-nathalie-sinclair-research-mathematics-ambassador.html |website=sfu.ca |accessdate=November 12, 2019 |date=March 15, 2017}}</ref> Later that year, Sinclair was elected a Member of the College of New Scholars, Artists and Scientists of the [[Royal Society of Canada]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Nathalie Sinclair Inducted into Royal Society of Canada |url=https://www.sfu.ca/education/news-events/2017/nathalie-sinclair-inducted-into-royal-society-of-canada.html |website=sfu.ca |accessdate=November 12, 2019 |date=September 12, 2017 }}</ref> In 2019, Sinclair was awarded the Svend Pedersen Lecture Award.<ref>{{cite web |title=Svend Pedersen Lecture Award 2019 - to Nathalie Sinclair |url=https://www.mnd.su.se/english/about-us/events/the-svend-pedersen-lecture-award/svend-pedersen-lecture-award-2019-to-nathalie-sinclair-1.422121 |website=mnd.su.se |accessdate=November 12, 2019}}</ref>
